static_traits.name: Lin Yue
static_traits.social_status: has friends to discuss personal matters with, but has not yet discussed worries about Student grades with them
static_traits.medical_history: no significant physical illness; no prior psychotherapy history; no similar problems in teaching career before
static_traits.language_features: clear expression, fairly high cooperativeness; repeatedly uses worry, helplessness and other emotional vocabulary; tends toward self-blame and negative Anticipation; can decompose problems and brainstorm in counseling, but skeptical of solutions

basic_info.main_problem: I worry my Students score below Anticipation on English tests, and I fear for their future.
basic_info.core_demands: recent exam results significantly affected my mental health, seeking counseling to cope with worries about Students.

core_beliefs: Students' substandard grades are my fault

special_situations.event: After English test scores were announced, most Students scored below Anticipation
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If Student scores are not good, it means I failed, I am not competent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Adding after-school tutoring, revising lesson plans to make up for insufficiencies
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It is my fault, their future will be terrible

special_situations.event: Teaching or preparing for exams in the English classroom, facing more difficult material
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my efforts cannot quickly improve scores, it proves I am incapable, nothing I do is of any use
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly adjusting lesson plans, but doubting the results, finding it hard to stick with systematic evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No matter what I do, nothing will change

special_situations.event: Considering introducing new methods for Students such as online resources or Learning groups
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If Students are not proactive enough or not interested, then all Interventions will fail
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Preemptively negating new methods or staying conservative, reducing investment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will not be interested or actively participate in these resources

special_situations.event: Choosing not to talk when having the chance to confide worries about Student scores to friends
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I express worries, others will think I am not professional, not competent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids discussing this matter with friends to escape being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am incompetent

core_conflict.wish: Longing to become a reliable Teacher who can ensure Student success, recognized as competent and effective
core_conflict.fear: Fearing Student failure and blaming oneself, being seen by others as not competent
defense_goal: Through doubled effort and self-reproach, maintains a sense of control, avoiding exposing vulnerability to keep a professional image

object_relations.self_representation: A savior/guardian bearing full responsibility for Students
object_relations.object_representation: Vulnerable Students needing to be fully prepared and protected by oneself

object_relations.self_representation: A Teacher who may be judged, not good enough
object_relations.object_representation: Others/friends who would evaluate one's professional ability

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When advised to try new teaching strategies or resources
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to think 'these methods will not work either', to avoid facing the sense of failure again
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Maintain Empathy and support, gently probe for specific evidence and details of past attempts; use open-ended questions to help them take small steps of evaluation and experimentation, avoiding directly negating their worries.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: After seeing Students' low scores or talking about exam failures
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Attributing failure entirely to oneself, thinking 'It is all my fault'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Conduct responsibility reattribution and fact-checking in a low-intensity, steady tone, encouraging them to distinguish controllable from uncontrollable factors, and Guidance them to form specific, actionable improvement plans.

manifestations: Feeling helpless in English class, believing efforts can hardly produce change
Holding pessimistic and 'fatalistic' views of Students' future
Holding skeptical and negating attitudes toward new plans
outcomes: Declining focus in teaching and lesson prep

contact_model.definition: The individual has poor self-Reflection and self-reproach, including excessive self-limitation and overcaution.
manifestations: Frequently blaming oneself and attributing poor scores entirely to oneself
Over-scrutinizing plans' feasibility, lowering willingness to try
Worrying about being seen as not competent

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from inside or outside, intentionally avoiding direct contact.
manifestations: Although having friends to talk to, avoiding discussing worries about Student scores
In social settings, avoids deeply touching on sources of stress

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others.
manifestations: Presupposing Students will not be interested or actively participate in new resources, attributing one's own doubts and disappointment to Students' insufficient motivation

positive_force: Has willingness to act (has already started extra tutoring sessions and revised lesson plans)
Can do problem decomposition and plan evaluation together with the counselor
Has some social support (friends to talk to)
Willing to try setting short-term goals and monitoring progress
negative_force: Self-reproach and excessive attribution to oneself
Holding doubt and negation toward new strategies, reducing investment in trying
Sleep disturbed and Decreased interest weakening energy and resilience
Avoids seeking support from friends, causing stress internalization

target_behavior.behavior: Excessive worry and self-reproach (accompanied by Anxiety and helplessness)
antecedent: Seeing or recalling low English test scores
When teaching in an English classroom
target_behavior.core_reason: Over-internalization of teaching responsibility and catastrophic thinking (believing Student scores are entirely attributable to oneself, and the future will surely be worse)
target_behavior.function: Maintains a sense of control through worry and self-criticism, tries to prevent failure and damage to self-evaluation
target_behavior.consequence: Declining focus in teaching and lesson prep,Sleep disturbance,Decreased interest,increased overall psychological burden

target_behavior.behavior: Social avoidance (not discussing worries about Student scores with friends)
antecedent: When there is a chance to confide stress and worries to friends
When asked about recent Work or Student performance
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying about being judged as not competent, fearing exposure of vulnerability and loss of control
target_behavior.function: Escaping shame and negative evaluation, maintaining a superficial professional image
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced access to support and outside resources, pressure accumulating inside, Anxiety maintained or worsened
